plain: To weigh something down, such as property with debts or claims

webster.text: To load; to clog; to impede motion with a load, burden or any thing inconvenient to the limbs; to render motion or operation difficult or laborious.

more.text: To embarrass; to perplex; to obstruct.
To load with debts; as, an estate is encumbered with mortgages, or with a widow's dower.

example.quote: And will he not, from his own interest in that species of property, be sufficiently prone to resist every attempt to prejudice or encumber it?
